ana: Quick proposal — to avoid a massive historical backfill for console telemetry v2 I want to try an 'oracle' read-adapter pattern. Keep existing rows, introduce a projection layer that maps old shape -> new shape at query time. Low-risk, faster rollout. :thinking_face:

ana: Rough idea: write a SQL view + small adapter in the query-service to synthesize missing fields. For dashboards we can materialize hot queries later. Example SQL view:```sql
CREATE VIEW analytics.v2_events AS
SELECT
  id,
  ts,
  COALESCE(payload->>'attrs', payload->>'attributes') AS attrs_json,
  -- legacy keys mapped
  COALESCE(route_id, route) AS route_id
FROM analytics.events;
```

kevin: I like avoiding full backfill. main concerns: query perf and index use. If we do COALESCE on JSON fields we'll likely miss indexes. how do we keep p99s? :eyes:

ana: Good call. Plan A: view + read-time mapping for correctness and rollout. Plan B: for heavy dashboards, create a small materialized table refreshed incrementally (or streaming CDC) for high-traffic slices. That keeps p99s tight.

mei: Another option is dual-write at ingest for a short window: new shape + legacy shape. That gives us a forward copy so reads can hit the new shape soon. downside: complexity for producers.

sam: +1 to dual-write but we must version the ingest API header so old clients don't break. propose header `X-Telemetry-Schema: v2` and a server-side adapter.

jules: Watch out for dashboard UX: some cards will be reading aggregated fields that don't exist in v1. If we mix reads across read-adapter and materialized tables we might show inconsistent numbers during rollout. Need clear gating or fallback for dashboards.

ana: Agreed. My suggested rollout timeline:
1) deploy read-adapter/view behind a feature flag — correctness only, no dashboard switch.
2) enable dual-write for new clients + a small percentage of traffic (canary).
3) run materialized refresh pipeline for top 10 dashboards (based on queries-per-hour) — can be incremental CDC -> table.
4) flip dashboard to v2 once materialized p99s are OK.

kevin: For step 3 can we precompute grouping keys so queries don't touch JSON path ops? e.g. store attrs_map as native columns for the most-used keys. That will limit cardinality explosion but keep speed.

mei: I can run a cohort analysis to find top N attr keys. quick SQL to sample:```sql
SELECT jsonb_object_keys(payload->'attributes') AS key, count(*)
FROM analytics.events
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
I'll return a list by EOD.

sam: ops side — if we dual-write we need to be careful: duplicate writes could cause idempotency issues downstream (billing, metrics). can we make new write idempotent by writing by event_id + schema_version?

ana: yes, adopt (event_id, schema_version) PK for materialized shards. For the legacy table we keep current PK. We'll add a lightweight migration layer that dedups on write.

jules: rollback story? if the read-adapter or materialized refresh reveals data skew we need a fast rollback. feature-flagging the dashboard is fine. but how fast can we stop dual-write? operators need a kill switch.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary plan created for branch feature/telemetry-v2-oracle — 3 hosts in prod-canary group. CI green.

kevin: Perf guardrails: if adapter adds >10% cpu to query-service or increases median latency by >20ms we'll pause. Also add a query-timer metric (telemetry.v2.adapter.latency) and a cardinality metric for any promoted attrs.

ana: noted. We'll add tracing tags so we can correlate queries that went through view vs materialized table.

mei: volunteering to prototype the read-adapter as a tiny express middleware that rewrites row shapes for the console query-service. I'll push a spike branch and link it here.

sam: I'll draft the ingest API header change and a backwards-compatible server-side flag. Also add a migration playbook: dual-write -> cutover -> stop legacy writes.

jules: Who owns the dashboard gating and QA? we need product signoff before flipping any dashboard. request: create a rollback dashboard (v2 vs v1 diff) so PMs can see drift.

ana: action items:
- mei: run attr-key frequency sample (SQL) and prototype adapter spike (deadline: EOD+2)
- sam: ingest header + idempotency plan + playbook (EOD+3)
- kevin: perf guardrail config + metric names (EOD+2)
- jules: QA checklist + dashboard drift diff dashboard (EOD+4)
- ana: implement view + feature-flag hook in query-service (I'll open PR today)

kevin: one more ask — include a cost estimate for materialized table storage and CDC throughput. we can budget it under console infra for the quarter.

ana: will add rough numbers in the PR description. thanks all. :tada:

jules: +1 — prefer the low-risk approach. let's not schedule a full backfill unless we absolutely must.

ops-bot: alert-bot: canary deployment started for feature/telemetry-v2-oracle at 1768004520 on prod-canary-1..3

ana: noted deploy start. will monitor metrics.

mei: uploaded spike branch: git link https://git.internal/r/telemetry-oracle-spike (contains view + small node adapter).

sam: opened ingest spec PR: https://git.internal/r/ingest-telemetry-schema-v2 (includes header + idempotency notes).

kevin: logging TODO — emit whether a row was mapped by read-adapter or read-from-materialized so we can sample errors.

ana: logging + trace flags added to the spike. closing loop: if all canary metrics look OK after 24h we move to 5% dual-write and start materializing top dashboards. otherwise rollback.

jules: thanks. ping me in #product when the diff dashboard is live.

ana: will do. end.
